summary: Live traffic: request to safely step back prefetch eviction + aggressive quantization after p95 latency surge
description: Customer reported a sudden increase in tail latency (p95 and p99) for inference calls after enabling an experiment that combined session coalescing, aggressive prefix-KV prefetching, and mixed-precision quantization. They request stepwise assistance to revert the optimizer changes for their tenant without traffic loss and with minimal token cost impact.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant enabled optimizer profile: session_coalesce=true, prefetch_mode=aggressive, quant_mode=auto-8bit via console UI
2) Traffic served through Dedicated pool (gpu-pool-dedicated-12) and observed response time increases within 5-15 minutes
3) Customer attempted a manual revert of prefetch_mode to 'balanced' which caused partial 5xx errors on long sessions
4) Reproduction verified on customer's traffic slice via shadow traffic in staging replica with similar P95 increase
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:23Z ERROR serving-runtime request_id=8a2b.. drop-kv-evict: eviction loop exceeded threshold on host gpu-12-03
2026-03-10T14:13:05Z WARN scheduler tenant=medlab shard=5 queue_delay_ms=1800 batch_size=1
2026-03-10T14:13:06Z INFO optimizer config_change user=medlab prefetch_mode=aggressive -> applied
investigation_notes: - Telemetry shows p95 increased from ~220ms to ~940ms within the first 10 minutes after profile flip.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked; memory pressure on GPU instances led to smaller effective batch sizes and higher per-token scheduling overhead.
- Long-lived sessions (seq_len > 1024) were disproportionately affected; these sessions also triggered fallback I/O which increased latency further.
- Manual revert attempts caused a config drift between control-plane and dataplane (some nodes saw old config, others new) producing transient 5xx during reconciliation.
- No underlying hardware failures detected; capacity was steady and no GPU OOMs were logged.
- Related console audit shows the change originated from customer engineer via web UI at 2026-03-10T14:12:58Z
hypothesis: 1) Aggressive prefetch + 8-bit quantization increased GPU memory churn and triggered frequent KV evictions, invalidating cached prefixes and forcing re-computation.
2) The combination led to reduced batching efficiency (many small batches), increasing scheduler overhead and queue delay.
3) Partial control-plane to data-plane configuration reconciliation caused inconsistent optimizer behavior per host and transient 5xx when handlers rejected requests during reconfiguration.
4) Long sessions exacerbate the memory pressure; short sessions not impacted as severely.
actions_taken: 2026-03-10T14:30Z - Support created snapshot of tenant optimizer profile and stored in tenant-snapshots (snapshot-id: snap-925471-1)
2026-03-10T14:35Z - Implemented traffic-split: 80% main path, 20% shadow with previous stable profile to verify behavior under real traffic
2026-03-10T14:42Z - Rolled prefetch_mode from 'aggressive' -> 'conservative' on a staged subset of hosts (shards 0-3) to observe impact
2026-03-10T15:00Z - Observed p95 decrease on staged hosts to ~260ms; started staged roll to remaining shards with 10min observation windows
2026-03-10T15:20Z - To avoid control-plane drift, applied coordinated two-step update: (1) mark maintenance flag for tenant, (2) push config and confirm via dataplane-ack endpoint
2026-03-10T15:35Z - Full revert to prior quant_profile (auto-16bit) applied after confirmation of snapshot integrity
2026-03-10T15:45Z - Cleared maintenance flag and resumed normal routing; customer advised to hold off on re-enabling quant_mode until we provide recommended profile settings
next_steps: - Run targeted load test with tenant shadow traffic + proposed conservative optimizer profile (session_coalesce=staged, prefetch_mode=balanced, quant_mode=16bit) and verify p95 under 300ms for 30 minutes
- Provide customer with a preflight checklist and a safe toggle script that performs snapshot -> staged apply -> verify -> rollout with automatic rollback on error
- Add a guard in the control plane: block simultaneous toggles that change prefetch+quant for tenants with >5% long-session traffic until a dry-run completes
- Follow up with a formal post-incident summary and an entry in the runbook library (confluence) with step-by-step commands used
- Schedule a 1:1 with MedLab infra team to review traffic patterns and recommend per-route optimizer profiles
